issues.legal_issue: A disputed tenancy’s genuineness must be determined through an inquiry in which the tenant can participate when the issue has not already been adjudicated.
material_facts: The dispute concerned whether a tenancy created in favour of the tenant was genuine or sham.
There had been no adjudication of the tenancy’s genuineness.
The bank submitted that the magistrate had considered the issue while deciding an intervention application.
The Court held that such consideration was insufficient and directed an inquiry with the tenant’s participation.
issues.conclusion: The magistrate must conduct an inquiry into the genuineness of the tenancy with the tenant’s participation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14 of the SARFAESI Act, the tenancy issue may be adjudicated before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. For a fair adjudication, consideration of the issue while deciding an intervention application is insufficient; an inquiry with the tenant’s participation is required.

predicates.secured_property_recovery_assistance_pro: The case concerns a magistrate’s role in assisting recovery of secured property.
predicates.tenancy_genuineness_disputed: A party disputes whether a tenancy concerning the property is genuine.
predicates.no_tenancy_adjudication: No adjudication has determined whether the tenancy is genuine.
predicates.issue_considered_only_in_intervention_ap: The tenancy issue was considered only while deciding an intervention application, rather than in an inquiry involving the tenant.

issues.definition: When a secured-property recovery assistance proceeding involves a disputed tenancy that has not been adjudicated and was considered only in an intervention application, a participatory tenancy inquiry is required.

issues.legal_issue: A pending inquiry into the genuineness of a tenancy does not prevent a lender from proceeding lawfully against the landlord.
material_facts: The Court directed an inquiry into the tenancy’s genuineness.
The Court clarified that the inquiry’s pendency would not stand in the way of the bank proceeding against the landlord in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The bank may proceed against the landlord in accordance with law while the inquiry is pending.
issues.legal_principle: The pendency of the tenancy inquiry does not prevent the bank from proceeding against the landlord in accordance with law.
